resources.string: After deploying a program, add its working directory and start command to manage it here.

Tasks run independently in Ubuntu and continue when you leave this page. Use foreground commands without &, nohup or daemon options. Programs already running in a terminal are not adopted. Tasks do not start automatically at boot.
Environment variables and multiple lines are supported. Use the terminal for interactive input.
Save, then start manually. Install the program and its dependencies in the terminal first.
The previous run did not finish normally. Review its logs before restarting.
Remove the configuration and logs for “%1$s”, stopping it first if running. Program files and the installation directory are kept.
No output yet. Some programs require unbuffered output for live logs, such as Python with -u.
Clear all logs for this task? Its process and program files are unaffected.
Only recent output within a size limit is retained; common credentials are redacted. Task commands and output are excluded from manager diagnostics.
Could not read task configuration. The original file is preserved. Retry and check free storage if this persists.
Task status could not be saved. Check free storage. The app still manages its process.
Up to %1$d tasks can be saved. Remove an unused task first.
Up to %1$d tasks can run at once. Stop another task first.
Use a name of 1–60 characters, without line breaks or control characters.
Enter an absolute Ubuntu path starting with /, without line breaks or control characters.
Enter a command of up to 32768 characters, without null characters.
Task not found. Return to the task list and retry.
Stop the task before editing it.
Could not start the task. Check Ubuntu initialization and free storage.
The task operation did not finish. Check free storage and retry.
Task output was interrupted and this task was stopped. Check free storage and retry.
Stopped for environment maintenance. Start manually after maintenance finishes.
The runtime service ended. Start the task manually to run it again.
